designImplications: P-END lever #1 — shrink the STORE FILE, not the end ext: every byte off the store is a byte off EVERY end-window contiguous ask (and every enable-drain read). Concrete diet: drop dead stats fields (buckets, pyramid, avgHr, avgMaxHr, avgHrr, activeHrr, peakSession, bestSessionHmRecent ~130-160B), slim or lazily-create s1-s9 (~800B for systems most users never touch), cap/trim projNames. Target: store well under 2KB so the end ask fits fragmentation holes that 2.2KB does not.

P-END lever #2 — cut the op COUNT: ext11 currently makes 4-5 whole-file-sized asks (2 reads + 2-3 writes). Restructure the RMW to 1 getObject + 1 setObject (e.g. fold the s<g> previous-session snapshot into the stats object, write pS<g> data inside stats) — halves the number of chances to hit the fatal alloc without changing what is persisted.

Kill the remaining grow-rewrite landmines: ship s1-s9 in the SAME shape ext11 writes (or make ext11 write only the shipped 5-field shape for systems with no extended data), so no first-end-on-new-system ever grows the file in the end window; treat companion projNames growth as a store-size budget item.

Do NOT add any LS write anywhere outside the end window on the theory that 'a small key is cheap' — c2e4e99 proved a ~100B setItem costs a full store-sized buffer. Any WAL/checkpoint idea inherits the whole-file cost; the mid-session and pause write bans stand, and even pause-time READS carry the same buffer cost (c76deac read storm).

M7 is dead as a design moment: getSummaryOutputs runs inside the same ~1s teardown as ext11 and the JS arena is discarded immediately after ('JS will discard'); the browsable recap is broker-served. Keep it RAM-only; never plan work there.

For the P-DIET architecture: proceed with the ext21-class satellite freely — the 08b crash is not a parse failure and does not indict M4 press-time parses. gradeName+buildSummary should stay RESIDENT (they run in the pause/end path where adding a compile-family risk on top of the existing LS-family risk is the only way to make things worse); their 1456B is the price of a storm-free fold. The end window's ext11 parse itself has never been the failing alloc — replacing it with resident code buys ~0 direct risk reduction, but shrinking its LS chain does.

Expand the zero-risk early-return: finishSession already skips the whole burst for routeless/clean sessions — extend change-detection so unchanged stats/s<g>/pS<g> values skip their setObject entirely (fewer file-sized asks per typical session).

Candidate on-watch experiment (hypothesis): heap-hole reservation — hold a ~2.5KB dummy allocation from onLoad, free it in finishSession right before loadExt(11); with the whole-file buffer model this converts the end-window lottery into a reserved contiguous hole. Needs a dedicated probe build + the 3-app log protocol before trusting it.

Accept that a fatal end storm is unrecoverable in code: try/catch demonstrably does not catch the allocator death spiral (08b hung to bootloop with catches in place), and RelMem cannot reclaim co-app memory synchronously. Prevention (store diet, op-count cut, no-growth) is the only defense; there is no graceful-degradation path to design for.

verdicts.jsallocIsWriteBuffer: CONFIRMED with refinement: the failing chunk is the whole-store-FILE access buffer (~file size +17-25B), charged on EVERY localStorage op — writes (c2e4e99: 2071 at the eP setItem BEFORE the ext11 evalFile line; grow-writes 2142/2148) AND reads (c76deac: 2056 = 2035B shipped data.jsn +21 at an enable-time getObject; 02.07 re-enable drains 2933/2163). It is NOT the ext11 parse: no storm value across 10 events matches ext11's 1055-1082B or a compile multiple, and 08b lacks the 'failed to eval' marker that identifies the separate compile-buffer family (ext12 2508/1518B; loader 1964/2392). 08b's 2230 = current store 2213B (+17) failing INSIDE the running RMW, on its first LS op.
verdicts.storeSizeHistory: The failing chunk tracks the STORE size at every era, never the code: 2933 (legacy rou-format store, 02.07) -> 2163 (post-rewrite store, SAME BUILD same evening — the single killing datapoint for the parse theory) -> ~2070/2071/2073 (03.07-06.07 stable era store) -> 2056 (c76deac fresh 2035B +21) -> 2142/2148 (06.07 grow-writes from the fresh 1820B built data.jsn) -> 2230 (08.07, shipped 2213B +17). ext11 meanwhile only moved 1082->1055B and main.js 8700->5861->7784->6302B with zero correlation. Note: installs do NOT wipe the store (the 2933 legacy store survived the 02.07 reinstall; ext13 migration exists for exactly this reason), so the store, not the build, is the persistent variable.
verdicts.endCleanConditions: The pause->end gap is NOT the discriminator: clean full-RMW ends at 1s/3s/4s/9s gaps (d702310, 02.07 fresh-install, 07d 39-min t3, 299100c) vs storms at 8s/12s gaps (c2e4e99, e3e3070). Clean requires two things: (1) the rewrite must not GROW the file — grow-rewrites (first-write growth, WAL-arm, seedSys) storm quasi-deterministically and were fixed by pre-population; (2) >= store-size contiguous headroom in the shared arena at the first LS op — 08b was a same-size RMW with zero corpses, ONE route, a clean triple-enable, and a completed pause-fold, killed purely by headroom collapse after 1h04 of MAPS+co-app churn at the 97-99% baseline. Severity follows retry depth: x3-retry storms survived to 'Exercise stopped', x11-retry storms are fatal (hang -> no ExSaving -> FS ASSERT at cable-plug -> bootloop), and RelMem force-unloading co-apps reclaims nothing synchronously, so once the storm starts mid-teardown there is no rescue.

designs.architecture:
PHILOSOPHY: the 08b bootloop was an LS-buffer failure (JSalloc:2230 = store file 2213B+17), not a parse failure — so this design keeps the proven end choreography move-for-move (pause-fold -> deLoad -> ONE sequential ext11 parse -> RMW) and attacks only its DEMAND: fewer whole-file asks, a smaller file, zero in-window growth, byte-parity parse. The diet comes from the already-measured D2 satellite motion (ext21 + ext14-wCm) plus moving gradeName (533B) out via per-system name-slice satellites at the proven route-commit moment; buildSummary+foldRoutes deliberately STAY resident (they run in the pause/end path — the one place where adding compile-family risk on top of the LS-family crash site is forbidden).

THREE MOVES, ALL BUILT AND MEASURED (sources: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-skyfi-Documents-suuntoapps-climb-logger/2039e491-48d8-49de-a28c-3c18d8e3dbc2/scratchpad/a3app, build in .../build-a3/climbl01-q.fea — Build successful, validateFile=true, output-lint clean):

(1) STORE CONSOLIDATION (P-END core). All internal per-system state moves into ONE stats key per system: stats.x<g> = 33-slot CSV string ([0..3] totalRoutes/totalSends/sessions/totalHeight accumulators, [4..12] the 9 legacy pass-through snapshot fields, [13..32] the 20-slot project vector). s0..s9 slim to their exact 5-field companion-contract shape (s0: 259B->79B); pS0..pS9 retired (no pS write ever again); dead never-written stats fields (buckets, avgHrr, activeHrr, peakSession) dropped from the shipped store. data.jsn: 2213B -> 1836B (-17%). ext11's chain collapses from 2 reads + 2-3 writes to 1 getObject(stats) + setObject(s<g>) + setObject(stats) — 3 asks steady-state, writes ORDERED so the shrinking write precedes the growing one (peak migration ask ~2140B < today's fatal 2230B). Both end-window growth landmines die: the s<g> 14-field first-end grow (+180B) and the pS<g> creation (+144B) are structurally impossible (write shapes <= shipped shapes). Lifetime file ceiling: ~2.1-2.2KB vs today's unbounded march to ~3.8KB. Bonus: the enable drain needs ONE getObject (stats) instead of two post-migration — the c76deac enable-read-storm class shrinks too. Migration is INSIDE ext11's existing single parse (x<g> undefined -> read old s<g>[+pS<g> only when clean]), once per system, ask count 4-5 = parity with today's EVERY end, then permanently 3. A 20,000-trial lockstep oracle (a3app/tools/tests/ext11-restructure-equiv.js) proves old-vs-new contract equality (all stats.*/s<g>.* companion fields, p<g>_* settings, purge ordering, post-switch history-preserve semantics) on both fresh installs and upgrade-in-place over the user's old store shape.

(2) ext11 BYTE-PARITY (M6). Restructured ext11 builds to 1055B vs master's 1056B — the compile arena ask is unchanged. Achieved by moving the slot-purge and the active* computation RESIDENT into finishSession (pure in-RAM data, a 4-slot array — no allocation class change in the window), which the oracle showed is also required for exact purge->active* ordering. NO second end ext ever (ext22 and any migration-sibling idea rejected per M6); getSummaryOutputs stays RAM-only (M7 dead).

(3) gradeName -> M8 NAME-SLICE SATELLITES (P-DIET). ext30..ext39 (one per grade system, 23-183B each — BELOW the proven 229B parse class) each return one flat CSV string of that system's grade names, generated in lockstep from master's gradeName (generator asserts equality for all systems x all indices). Parsed ONCE per session at the first commitDirty, sequentially right after the proven f10 parse; the returned string (nmS, <=190 chars) stays resident for the session (survives pause — it is a string, not a parse cache); the fn ref is dropped immediately. On throw: nmS stays null, natural retry at the next commit, no timers. buildSummary indexes nmS at fold time — always consistent with acc[6] (no staleness under EDIT/quickfix mutations, unlike best-name-at-commit variants). buildSummary itself is rewritten data-driven (row specs in one split string) and stays resident, called at pause-fold and end-fold exactly as master. ext18 (dead payload, no call site) and ext22 are deleted; ext21/ext14 carried over from D2 unchanged (60k-trial oracle green, off-watch only).

RESULT: main.js blob 7191B (master 7784B, -593B), end window strictly reduced on every axis, zero nominal UX delta. The remaining ~700B gap to the 6.3-6.5KB floor is exactly the resident buildSummary+foldRoutes that M5/M6/M7 pin; two PROBE-GATED stage-2 options are specified (not committed): (S2a) after the M8-band probe proves ~700B parses, fold the row-builder into ext10 (f10 is provably alive at every acc-changing fold if the pause handler folds before nulling f10) -> ~6.74KB; (S2b) a D1-class edit-overlay-entry satellite for the remaining EDIT/proj action bodies -> ~6.4KB. Neither may proceed on the corpse-roulette rationale alone: the A1 gate analysis showed even -48% blob only scales the toggle threshold (1->5 corpses), so end-safety, not the diet, is this design's payload.

designs.endWindowPlan:
CHOREOGRAPHY: unchanged move-for-move from master (commitDirty [+f10 parse only if a route is mid-climb — existing master behavior] -> foldRoutes+buildSummary resident -> early-return if nothing to save -> deLoad -> f10/fE=null -> resident purge + A-block -> single try/catch'd loadExt(11) -> sequential LS ops inside).

BEFORE (master on the user's watch; store 2213B shipped, 2230B measured at 08b):
- Parse demand: ext11 1056B source -> compile-family arena ~1.7-2.1KB transient (chunk ratio 1.6-2x per the ext12/loader storm data).
- Store demand: getObject(stats) + getObject(s<g>) + [setObject(pS<g>) if dirty] + setObject(stats) + setObject(s<g>) = 4-5 whole-file contiguous asks x ~2230B. Cumulative window churn ~11-13KB.
- In-window growth landmines: first end on a new system grows the file +~180B (14-field s<g>) plus +~144B (pS<g> creation) — the storm class that killed c2e4e99/4df2481-#1.
- Lifetime trajectory: store marches toward ~3.8KB (10x 259B s<g> + pS creations), so EVERY future ask grows even with frozen code.

AFTER (measured build):
- Parse demand: ext11 1055B built = BYTE-PARITY (-1B). Arena ask unchanged. No second end parse of any kind.
- Store demand steady-state: 1 getObject(stats) + setObject(s<g>) + setObject(stats) = 3 asks. Fresh store 1836B -> asks ~1850-1950B (worst single ask -370B / -16.6% vs 2230). User's migrated store settles ~2100B -> 3 asks x ~2120B. Cumulative window churn ~7.8-8.4KB (-35%).
- Migration ends (once per system, existing stores): 4-5 asks at the old ~2230B class — COUNT parity with today's every-end; write order (s<g> shrink-write BEFORE the x<g>-adding stats write) caps the peak single ask at ~2140B, BELOW today's fatal 2230B. After the first migration end the file drops ~90-190B and keeps shrinking as further systems migrate.
- Landmines: s<g> growth ELIMINATED (write shape <= shipped shape, s0 shrinks 259->~80B), pS creation ELIMINATED (no pS writes exist). Sole residual: one-time stats.x<g> value creation (+~90B) per system, deliberately ordered onto the just-shrunk file.
- Enable-window co-benefit (same buffer physics): drain does 1 getObject instead of 2 once x<g> exists — halves the c76deac-class enable-read exposure.
- Early-return extension: unchanged from master (routeless+clean sessions skip the burst entirely); with the consolidated store a slots-only or system-only session is 1R+2W instead of today's 4.
- Explicitly NOT done: no LS anywhere else (pause/tick/summary writes stay banned), no headroom-reservation hack (logged as a separate probe candidate for the orchestrator, untested), no getSummaryOutputs work (M7 dead).

designs.name: Designer B — MOMENT-SHIFT "Stage-Left": commit-staged end satellite + drain read-shift + pause headroom reserve + M7 recap (probe built+measured 6724B)
designs.architecture:
PHILOSOPHY: the end window keeps ONLY what physically cannot leave it — the whole-store setObject writes (END is the only persistence moment on this watch: drain writes proven non-persistent, mid-session/pause writes proven toxic). Everything else that today executes between 'Disable' and 'Exercise stopped' is shifted to earlier, proven moments, and every shifted element degrades to today's exact behavior on failure (a strict-fallback lattice: the design can never make an end WORSE than master).

THE FOUR SHIFTS (on top of the D2 base = ext21 EDIT-satellite + ext14+wCm + ext22 content extracted, measured 6375B):
1. READ-SHIFT (end reads → M1 drain): drainF12 retains the stats object it already reads (statsRAM) and re-adds the s<gs> getObject (tRAM) — this RESTORES the months-proven ext12-era drain read set (stats/s<gs>/pS<gs>), it is not a new moment. pendSlots' calm-tick read refreshes both after a system switch. finishSession hands both to ext11 as params; ext11 keeps `v=v||getObject(...)` fallback reads, so a failed drain collapses to today's path. Removes 2 of the 4-5 whole-store contiguous asks (JSalloc≈2230 class, per the forensics' per-op buffer model) from the end window.
2. PARSE-SHIFT (end evalFile → M8 route-commit piggyback): commitDirty arms pendStage after each successful commit until fS11 is cached; evaluate parses ext11 ONE tick later (pendSlots choreography — never at the press, never per-press, one-shot per session), and fS11 is deliberately NOT freed at pause: its ~1KB compiled residency replaces the ~2.07KB end-window parse arena (08b reading: the end parse SUCCEEDED and likely consumed the very hole the first 2230B store ask then missed — removing the parse un-eats that hole). Every session that needs the fold/RMW (≥1 route) has by construction had a commit = a staging opportunity, with natural per-commit retry. Fallback: `(fS11 || loadExt(11))` at end = today's window exactly. This is precisely the "route-commit piggyback" carrier the evidence phase nominated; the 650-950B+ band question is checkpoint-gated.
3. SUMMARY-SHIFT (recap rows → M7, evaluated per mission): ext22 (gradeName + row build, unchanged content) is NEVER parsed in the end window anymore (D2's end-sibling call — the explicitly killed idea — is deleted). getSummaryOutputs builds lastSummaryCache lazily via one try/catch'd loadExt(22) AFTER the save completes — the months-proven ext9 recap moment, used exactly as the evidence graded it: cosmetic-only, never persistence; a throw degrades to a resident Sends/Routes row built from acc with REAL numbers (better than master's 0/0 default). foldRoutes stays RESIDENT (the storm-free fold/free of routesA/B at pause is the safety valve; honoring the evidence phase's core concern — nothing in the pause/end path ever compiles).
4. HEADROOM-SHIFT (the pendSlots-spirit reservation, hypothesis-grade): onExercisePause — immediately after deLoad frees the ~13KB active.html — builds a 3072-char string reserve (contiguous, refcount-freed; log-doubling from a 24-char literal, ~60B source). finishSession releases it as the LAST act before the LS burst, so the first ~2230B store-buffer ask lands in a pre-cut 3072B hole instead of playing the fragmentation lottery. Freed on continue (never held while climbing); try/catch'd (OOM → proceed as today). Heap-alloc only: no LS, no parse — same M5 class as foldRoutes' acc allocation.

IDEAS EVALUATED AND REJECTED (with the honest re-examination the mission asked for):
- Write stats at M7/getSummaryOutputs: DEAD for writes — M7 fires inside the same ~1s teardown ('JS will discard' follows within seconds; in 08b it was mid-storm), and c2e4e99 proved ANY setItem charges a whole-store buffer, so moving the write 2s later reduces nothing and adds a race with the arena discard. Adopted for the cosmetic row build only.
- Apply-pending-at-next-enable-drain: the falsification's failure mode (replay-at-enable-PARSE + pause-window WAL write) is indeed distinct from this variant — but it dies on three independent proven facts anyway: (a) drain writes do not persist (stats.mig latch vanished, log 07b) → the pending key can never be cleared nor the fold checkpointed → double-apply; (b) the end still needs ≥1 whole-store ask to write even a ~100B pending key (c2e4e99) → ZERO end-window demand reduction; (c) companion stats stale until the NEXT session's end → violates companion-current-after-save. Rejected without needing the historical falsification.
- Pre-write invariant parts at pause (same-size rewrite): no evidence supports relaxing the M5 write ban (the only pause write ever shipped froze the watch); a pause write faces the same whole-store contiguous ask on the same churned heap ~3s earlier (zero reduction), and a resume forces a second end write (doubled exposure + reconciliation). Dropped.
- Build summary at the LAST route commit: 'last commit' is unknowable in advance; adopted in modified form — inputs (acc) fold incrementally at pause/end exactly as today, the row build moves to M7, and the real commit-moment win is staging the end-write satellite at the FIRST commit.

08b COUNTERFACTUAL: enable 10:00:52 → drain reads 3 keys (proven class, clean heap); commit 11:05:01 (ext10 parse clean — proven in that log); 11:05:02 fS11 staged; pause 11:05:05 deLoad frees ~13KB → reserve carves 3072B of it; end 11:05:08: zero parse, zero reads, reserve released, the single fatal-class 2230B ask lands in the pre-cut hole. Two independent defenses where master had none. Honest caveat: if the 11:05:02 staging parse had failed (band question), the reserve alone must carry a fallback parse (2070B arena) + writes — the hole covers one, not both, so the double-jeopardy path is only ~1-2 asks better than today.

COMPOSITION: orthogonal to the store diet (Designer A class) — every byte off data.jsn shrinks BOTH the remaining write asks and the required reserve; the s1-s7 14-field first-end growth landmine and companion projNames growth are inherited unchanged and stay owned by that design. ext18 (dead payload, no call site) is deleted. designs.endWindowPlan: BEFORE (master, typical route session, from the 08b/forensics model): 1× evalFile ext11 = ~2.06-2.07KB contiguous arena (JSalloc:2070 class), whose arena+compiled body then OCCUPY the heap for the rest of the window (08b reading: the parse succeeded and likely ate the hole the store buffer needed) + 2× getObject (stats, s<g>) + 2-3× setObject (pS<g> if dirty, stats, s<g>), EACH charging a whole-store contiguous access buffer ≈ 2.23KB (JSalloc:2230 = data.jsn 2213B+17) ⇒ 5-6 sequential ≥2KB contiguous asks, ~11.3-13.4KB cumulative transient demand, zero reserved headroom, no rescue path once one ask fails. AFTER (staged path = any session with ≥1 committed route, i.e. every session that has a fold to persist): parse bytes in window = 0 (fS11 cached since commit-tick+1; ext22 never parsed at end — even D2's sibling call is deleted); read asks = 0 (statsRAM/tRAM RAM handoff from the drain); write asks = 2-3 × ~2.23KB (unavoidable — END is the only persistence moment; keys/sizes unchanged, order now stats→s<g>→pS<g> so the companion-critical key persists first) — and immediately before the first ask a 3072B contiguous hole is released (pause-armed reserve, carved from deLoad's ~13KB the moment it was freed). Net: ask count 5-6 → 2-3, compile-family demand 2.07KB → 0, largest single ask unchanged at ~2.23KB but now smaller than the pre-cut hole. FALLBACK LADDER (never grows the window): staging failed → end parses ext11 as today, minus the 2 reads (RAM still valid) = today−2 asks; staging AND drain both failed → ext11's fallback reads fire = today's window byte-for-byte. Routeless dirty-only sessions (sysDirty/slotsDirty, no commit): no staging happened → fallback parse + 2-3 writes ≈ today−2 reads... reads skipped whenever the drain succeeded, which is the normal case. The whole-store ask SIZE itself is only reducible by the store diet — composes directly (every data.jsn byte cut shrinks all remaining asks AND the required reserve margin).

M2 (mounts) — COMPLIANT: no mount gains any allocation; goState untouched beyond D2's fE=null (a free); onExerciseContinue adds only resv=null (a free) BEFORE the remount; setup→ready confirm stays mount-only; the pendSlots read stays one tick after the mount and now also refreshes tRAM in the same already-budgeted read moment. M3 (fluid paths) — COMPLIANT: eid1/2/7/8 handlers and the per-tick setOutputs render are byte-identical to the D2 base; pendStage never gates onEvent (only pendF12/pendSlots do, as in master); zero per-press allocation added anywhere. M4 (action presses) — COMPLIANT with flags: ext14 (318B, proven class) and ext21 (645B, unproven band → checkpoint) parse at presses, cached-per-visit, released at exit/pause/end, every call try/catch'd no-op with natural press-again retry, no timers; call shapes are flat/by-ref with no inner fns and no output writes from exts. M5 (pause) — COMPLIANT: pause work = deLoad + f10/fE frees + RESIDENT foldRoutes (all proven) + ONE resident heap allocation (the reserve string — same allocation class as foldRoutes' acc; explicitly NOT a parse, NOT an LS read, NOT an LS write); nothing at pause assumes the session ends (resume frees the reserve, f10 re-parses lazily, fS11 simply stays cached); no parse was placed at pause despite the temptation — the no-precedent gap is respected. M6 (end window) — COMPLIANT, the core deliverable: the window LOSES its parse (staged at M8) and both reads (M1 handoff) in the normal path; D2's end-sibling ext22 parse — the explicitly killed 'add another end ext' idea — is deleted; nothing new is added; write count/keys/sizes unchanged (2-3 setObject) with companion-critical stats written first; every fallback path is ≤ today's window; the reserve release shrinks nothing but pre-cuts a hole larger than the largest remaining ask. M7 (getSummaryOutputs) — used exactly as the evidence graded it: cosmetic-only recap build on the months-proven ext9 precedent, AFTER persistence completes, try/catch'd, degrading to a resident row; NEVER persistence, no LS. M8 (route commit) — COMPLIANT+: ext10 unchanged at its proven 229B/lifecycle; the end-satellite staging piggybacks the commit MOMENT on the tick AFTER it (pendSlots choreography), one-shot per session with per-commit retry — this is the evidence phase's nominated 'route-commit piggyback' carrier, and its 1070B band question is the design's one gated experiment. CALL-SHAPE RULES — all satisfied: no per-call inner fns anywhere, by-ref mutation throughout (eBag/projSlot/routesA/B/statsRAM), object-graph returns only at rare moments (ext10 per-commit, ext22 once post-save), no ext writes outputs (main.js literal slot writes untouched), ext parse budgets all ≤1.6KB flat, dispatcher 1369B < 1874B, outputs unchanged/float32-safe, every press-time and staged evalFile try/catch'd with retry-by-natural-repetition and zero timers.

designs.name: C — CAPSULE STORE: freeze the file, fold the ops
designs.architecture:
PHILOSOPHY: the 08b forensics proved the end-window killer is the whole-store-FILE access buffer (JSalloc ~= data.jsn size +17-25B), charged on EVERY localStorage op, and that key-level splitting changes nothing — only (a) total file bytes and (b) op count matter. This design attacks both, then reuses the measured D2 satellite work for P-DIET since the two problems are independent failure families.

P-END: STORE REDESIGN (data.json 2213B -> 2016B shipped, growth-frozen)
1. DROP dead stats fields (measured 114B): buckets, pyramid, avgHr, avgMaxHr, avgHrr, activeHrr, peakSession, bestSessionHmRecent. Four of these are manifest variables that no shipped build has ever written (always 0/""): remove the store keys AND the 4 manifest variable entries in the same release — a coordinated, documented contract change, not a silent break. avgHrr/activeHrr/peakSession/buckets are in no contract at all.
2. DROP p8_*/p9_* slot mirrors (measured 100B): they are in NEITHER settings nor variables (companion never sees them); slot grades for systems 8/9 already live in the projSlot vector (indices 15-19), which persists via the new q capsule. fillSlots falls back to projSlot[15..19] for gs>=8 at drain. Zero behavior change.
3. q CAPSULE — pS<g> folded INTO stats as one pre-shipped string (105B, replaces pS0 142B + nine future +142B pS-create landmines): stats.q = ten ';'-joined systems of five ','-joined packed slot numbers, v = (att*1000+snd)*1e7 + bestTime*100 + (grade+1), empty slot = 0. Max (9999*1000+999)*1e7+8639900+42 ~= 1.0e14 < 2^53, exact in float64 (LS-internal, never crosses the float32 output transit). Saturation caps att<=9999/snd<=999 (absurd lifetimes; matches the packedBreak saturation precedent). KILLS the pS<g> setObject op at end AND the pS getObject at enable (drain reads stats ONLY: enable-window LS reads drop 2 -> 1, directly helping the c76deac-class enable-read exposure).
4. x CAPSULE — per-system history archive as one pre-shipped stats string (225B): ten ';'-joined systems of 'th,lsg,bo5,lpg,mtg,sap,bhm,lps,mtp'. This lets s0..s9 stay PERMANENTLY at their shipped 5-field contract shape ({totalRoutes,totalSends,sendPct,sessions,peakGrade|totalHeight}) — ext11 never again grows an s<g> from 5 to 14 fields, killing the +180B first-end-on-new-system landmine on all 9 systems while preserving full per-system history (zero feature loss). s0 shrinks 257B -> 77B.
5. sy MARKER (+8B): stats.sy = 'system these stat fields belong to', written only by ext11. stats.system is companion-writable, so it cannot serve as the self-consistency marker. When sy === gradeSystem (typical), stats' own 14 fields ARE the previous state and the s<g> read is skipped entirely; when sy !== g (system switched on watch or from phone), main.js normalizes sv once from s<g> + x[g] before calling ext11 (rare path, resident). Legacy 14-field s<g> objects self-heal: the switched-read prefers s<g>'s own fields when present, so pre-migration multi-system history flows into x[g] losslessly at that system's next end.
6. OP FOLD: end chain goes from 2 reads + 3 writes (5 whole-file buffers) to 1 read + 2 writes typical (3 buffers); routeless-but-dirty sessions 1R+1W; unchanged sessions keep the existing zero-op early return; the s<g> write is additionally skipped when that system had no routes and no history change.
7. LAZY v3 MIGRATION at first end (writes are only legal at end; c76deac bans enable writes): drainF12 keeps a legacy-compat read branch (sv.q undefined -> read old pS<gs>) for the one session between update and first end. finishSession reads stats once (resident), and iff sv.q === undefined parses ext16 (~420B, once ever per watch) which reshapes sv in RAM (seed q/x, delete dead keys and p8/p9 mirrors) and neuters pS0 to a scalar 0 (one extra write, once). Every write in the migration end SHRINKS the file (2213 -> ~2040) — the safe rewrite class; growth transients stay 0 per the 299100c doctrine. Fresh installs ship the new data.json and never migrate. x/q ship as STRINGS, so the VS-Code array-drop gotcha is avoided by construction; the pS0 neuter value is a scalar.

P-DIET: SATELLITE LAYOUT (independent of P-END per evidence; adopted from measured D2)
8. ext21 (D2, built + 60k-trial lockstep green): EDIT overlay engine + DEL + BREAK quickfix, entry-parsed at the eid5 press, cached per visit (fE), released at exit/pause/end, eBag reused 6-slot vector by-ref. Extended with the action-side of the PROJ overlay (eid6 slot-step, eid5 exit; the dy handler STAYS resident — M3 fluid) -> ~825B.
9. ext10 v2: gradeName + buildSummary ride the PROVEN route-commit parse (M8) as op-dispatched extensions of the existing commit engine (~1200B flat). The pause fold calls the ALREADY-CACHED f10 (op1) to build the summary — a session with routes has always parsed f10 by then; a session without routes needs no summary; the frDirty-at-pause case already parses f10 at end today (commitDirty), so NO new parse moment exists at pause or end. onExercisePause reorders to fold BEFORE f10=null. This answers the open gradeName+buildSummary placement question without touching the end window (ext22 stays dead per M6). foldRoutes, recalcBse, cycleSlot/toggleMode, setOutputs, drain stay resident (pinned).
10. ext18 deleted (869B dead .fea payload, no call site). ext12 remains deleted. ext13 updated to emit capsule shape (rou-era cold path, unreachable on current stores).

Fallback ladder if the R1 probe fails: ext10v2-lite = commit + gradeName only (780B, inside the weak-803 band), buildSummary resident (~6950B resident); worst case all-resident summary (~7350B, still below master). The heap-hole reservation experiment (hold ~2.2KB from onLoad, free before the first end op) remains an orthogonal, explicitly-hypothesis add-on and is NOT load-bearing here.

This is a once-ever controlled exception to 'no new end ext', not a permanent window occupant; the permanent window is strictly smaller than today's.

extLayout.cacheLifecycle: Uncached, at most once per legacy store lifetime.

designs.endWindowPlan:
BEFORE (master, byte-identical to the build that bootlooped in 08b): ext11 parse 1056B = one ~2.07KB contiguous compile arena (JSalloc:2070 class), THEN 4-5 whole-file LS buffers at 2230B each (getObject stats, getObject s<g>, conditional setObject pS<g>, setObject stats, setObject s<g>; store 2213B shipped +17 organic). Total contiguous churn ~11.0-13.2KB across 5-6 asks; max single ask 2230B. PLUS three live in-window GROWTH landmines (the quasi-deterministic storm class): +180B s<g> 5->14-field grow on the first end of any non-default system, +142B pS<g> file-key CREATION on the first project end per system, unbounded companion projNames growth. Store trajectory is structurally rising (2123 -> 2213 already; a multi-system project user trends toward ~2.9KB — the 02.07 legacy store stormed at exactly its own 2933B size).

AFTER (steady state): finishSession does 1 resident getObject(stats) at ~2033B buffer (2016B shipped +17), then ext11v2 parse <=1100B (arena <=~2.15KB, hard build gate) doing exactly 2 setObject at ~2033B each; typical total ~8.2KB across 4 asks (-35% churn, one fewer ~2.2KB-class ask); max single ask ~2.15KB arena / ~2.03KB store (store ask -8.8%). Switched-system sessions add one rare s<g> read (5 asks — still below today's typical). Routeless-but-dirty ends: 1R+1W. Unchanged sessions: existing zero-op early return, now extended with per-key change detection. ZERO in-window growth writes remain: every shape is pre-shipped and every write is a same-size-class rewrite (only string digit growth, ~+1-2B/field, the same organic class as the observed +17/+21). The demand CURVE is the real win: shipped 2016B, realistic heavy-lifetime ~2100-2150B (extreme all-10-systems-maxed bound: 2798B), versus today's structurally unbounded 2213 -> 2900B+ trajectory. Pause window unchanged (deLoad + resident foldRoutes + cached-f10 summary call, no LS, no parse).

MIGRATION END (once per watch, first end after update): 1R at legacy 2230B ask + ext16 parse (~420B, ~0.9KB arena) + pS0-neuter write + ext11 parse + 2W, on a file that SHRINKS from 2213B to ~2040B during the same end. Protocol requirement: the first post-update session is a deliberate SHORT one (2 minutes, 1 route) so the biggest legacy-sized asks land on a fresh, unchurned heap.
designs.estimateArithmetic: Anchors: master built blob 7784B (measured, unzip -p climbl01-q.fea main.js | wc -c); D2 variant BUILT+MEASURED 6375B with ext21+ext22 both externalized (net -1409B for EDIT cluster 906B + gradeName 533B + buildSummary ~400B bodies minus ~430B glue: eBag, fE cache mgmt, try/catch call sites, loadExt(22) site). Chain for this design: 7784 START; -656 EDIT cluster -> ext21 (D2-measured class: -906 body, +250 glue); -813 gradeName+buildSummary -> ext10v2 op1 (-933 bodies per inventory [533 gradeName + ~400 buildSummary-sans-foldRoutes, consistent with ext22's 1037B], +120 glue: op dispatch, pause f10-call + nR>0 guard, reorder); -220 PROJ-overlay action ops -> ext21 extension (-300 of the 505B project-editing cluster [dy handler ~150B stays resident, fluid-pinned], +80 glue); +410 capsule-store resident glue (drain q-decode +130, legacy pS-read kept as compat fallback +15 net vs deletion, fillSlots gs>=8 fallback +40, finishSession sv read/pass +60, switched-normalize rare path +180, ext16 gate line +55; the pendSlots path is untouched); +45 misc (sy handling, change-detect skips). TOTAL: 7784 - 656 - 813 - 220 + 410 + 45 = 6550B. Honest band 6400-6700 (glue estimates carry +-150B; every step is build-measured before deploy against the corpse ladder: 7784B fails at corpse #1, 6302B at ~#2-3). Store math (python-measured on constructed JSON): new data.json 2008B + 8B sy = 2016B vs 2213B today (-197B, -8.9%); components: dead fields -114, p8/p9 mirrors -100, pS0 -> q capsule -142+105, s0 slim -180, x capsule +225, sy +8, misc commas ±. Extreme-lifetime bound 2798B (all 10 systems at max digit width) vs today's unbounded landmine trajectory.
uxDeltas: Companion: 4 always-dead tiles removed (Send Pyramid, Avg HR, Avg Max HR, Best Recent Session Height) — no shipped build has ever written them (permanently 0/empty); removed from data.json AND manifest variables in the same release as a documented contract change. All live stats, settings paths (stats.system, stats.p0_1..p7_5, projNames0..7) and per-system tiles are byte-for-byte preserved.

Watch screens, flows, button semantics, summary rows, stats math: NONE (zero feature loss; ext21/ext10v2 are behavior-identical externalizations — D2's 60k-trial lockstep oracle pattern extends to the capsule encode/decode via the existing stats-endwrite-equiv and drain-inline-equiv harnesses).

Latency (imperceptible class, listed for honesty): first route commit per segment parses ~1200B instead of 229B on a non-interactive tick moment; EDIT/PROJ overlay entry gains a one-time ~825B parse per visit (D2-designed, pre-warmed at the entry press).

Saturation: per-slot lifetime attempts cap at 9999 (was ~unbounded int, display already capped at 16700) and sends at 999 in the packed q capsule — unreachable in real use, same class as the shipped packedBreak saturation.

risks.risk: ext10v2 ~1200B parse at route commit (M8) is in the UNPROVEN 950-1600B band (proven 229B, weak 803B) and re-fires after every pause.
risks.mitigation: Flat file, zero inner fns, cached per segment; fallback ladder pre-built: ext10v2-lite = commit+gradeName only (780B, weak band) with buildSummary resident (~6950B), worst case all-resident (~7350B, still under master).
risks.onWatchCheckpoint: Dedicated probe build FIRST (this is the exact probe the evidence phase called for): 3-app protocol, session with >=5 routes and >=2 pause/continue cycles; watch the commit ticks for JSalloc/RelMem lines; archive the log ring immediately; only then promote to the full build.

risks.risk: ext21 at 645-825B parses at an action press — the unproven 650-950 band (one weak-positive at 803B whose CALL, not parse, was the ext20 killer).
risks.mitigation: Allocation-light call shape already oracle-proven off-watch (eBag by-ref, flat results); pre-warm at entry so action presses hit the cache; try/catch + press-again everywhere; if the PROJ extension breaches 950B, ship the measured 645B EDIT-only version.
risks.onWatchCheckpoint: Overlay torture session: enter/exit EDIT and PROJ x20 mid-session, eid4 result-cycle spam, BREAK quickfix presses, one deliberate corpse-heap toggle before entry to verify the graceful no-op + retry path; freeze-taxonomy watch (THROW/HANG/EVICT), >=60s hands-off-cable if anything freezes.

risks.risk: ext11v2 size creep past 1056-1100B would GROW the end-window compile arena — violating the M6 no-growth law the whole design serves.
risks.mitigation: Hard build gate <=1100B (unzip -p .fea ext11.js | wc -c) wired into the pre-deploy checklist; the switched-normalize and migration already live outside ext11 to protect the budget; identifier-diet before any feature spill.
risks.onWatchCheckpoint: 3 short-session clean ends, then the 08b re-test scenario: 1h+ session with MAPS style/tile churn, Weather+Movement co-resident, single route committed ~T-7s, pause then end within 3s — must complete ExSaving with zero relMemCb storm; archive log.

risks.risk: The one-time migration end does its first LS ops at the LEGACY 2230B ask (same size as the 08b fatal ask) plus an extra ext16 parse.
risks.mitigation: Migration is shrink-only (every write reduces the file), fires once, and is user-schedulable; ext16 <=450B; drain compat branch means a failed migration retries at the next end harmlessly.
risks.onWatchCheckpoint: Controlled post-update protocol: first session deliberately 2 minutes / 1 route on a fresh boot, >=60s hands-off after save; verify next enable is clean, companion stats intact, and (via a follow-up build check or log JSalloc value at any later event) that the store now measures ~2040B.

risks.risk: Capsule decode/encode corruption (truncated q/x strings, foreign writes) could poison projSlot or history.
risks.mitigation: Drain decode fully try/catch'd with zero/-1 defaults (existing pendF12 backoff pattern); ext11 gates capsule ops on field presence; lockstep oracles extended: drain-inline-equiv + stats-endwrite-equiv must replay old-vs-new semantics over the migration boundary and 60k randomized sessions.
risks.onWatchCheckpoint: Sim corrupt-store matrix (empty q, short q, garbage x) then on-watch: fresh-flash enable, legacy-store enable, and post-migration enable all clean; slots and history verified on the READY/PROJ screens.

risks.risk: Companion interop: settings written from the phone (slot grades, projNames, system) between sessions must survive the new shapes; sy-marker must correctly flag phone-side system switches.
risks.mitigation: slotsDirty gating unchanged; stats rewrite is read-object pass-through so unknown/companion keys survive; sy is app-only by construction so a phone system switch forces the s<g>+x normalize path.
risks.onWatchCheckpoint: Round-trip test: edit a P-slot grade, a projName, and the grade system from the companion; sync; run a session; end; verify slots show the phone edits, the end write preserves them, and the new system's history seeded correctly from s<g>.

risks.risk: Residual 08b exposure: the design cuts the ask ~9% and the op exposure ~35-40%, but a sufficiently fragmented heap after 1h of co-app churn can still fail a ~2KB contiguous ask — prevention is probabilistic, not absolute, and a fatal storm remains unrecoverable in code.
risks.mitigation: This design is compatible with the orthogonal heap-hole reservation experiment (hold ~2.2KB from onLoad, free in finishSession before the first LS op) — explicitly flagged HYPOTHESIS, to be probed separately, never load-bearing here.
risks.onWatchCheckpoint: P-END is not declared closed until the long-session matrix passes: 30min and 60min sessions with map churn + both co-apps, ends at 3s and 10s pause gaps, all logs archived; any storm re-opens the reservation probe as the next lever.

risks.risk: fillSlots gs>=8 fallback and the drain q-decode change the bootstrap path that instant-start depends on (M1 is untouchable).
risks.mitigation: Mechanism unchanged (plain getObject + small allocations, one FEWER read than today); decode is a flat split/divide loop, no evalFile, no writes; lockstep oracle covers it.
risks.onWatchCheckpoint: Re-run the master-validation trio on the new build: instant-start, rapid enable/disable toggles, sport-switch — all must match the 07i/07j clean signatures, plus one hangboard session with configured slots ending and restoring across re-enable.

designs.momentRuleAudit:
M1 (enable/onLoad/first ticks): COMPLIANT, strictly improved. No evalFile added anywhere in the enable window; the hybrid inline getObject drain is untouched in mechanism; enable LS reads drop from 2 (stats + pS<gs>) to 1 (stats, with q/x decoded from the object already in hand) — reduced exposure to the c76deac enable-read storm class. The ext13 latent cold-migration exception is preserved unchanged (unreachable on current stores). No tick/timer-deferred work added; pendF12/pendSlots/skipP choreography byte-identical. Drain writes remain banned; the v3 migration deliberately does NOT write at drain.
M2 (mount moments): COMPLIANT. Zero new allocation at any template swap or overlay mount; the setup->ready confirm stays mount-only; pendSlots keeps exactly its single stats re-read one tick after the mount (an earlier design draft added a second read there — rejected; the switched-system s<g> read lives in the end window instead, where it replaces a read that always happened today).
M3 (fluid paths): COMPLIANT. eid1/2/7/8 handlers, cycleSlot, toggleMode, recalcBse, per-tick setOutputs render all stay resident and lock-free; EDIT/PROJ dy handlers stay resident even though their action siblings move to ext21; inside the EDIT overlay, eid1/2 hit the entry-cached fE (no parse, no per-press allocation, by-ref eBag).
